proximity

/prok-SIM-uh-tee/ — stress on second syllable · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Proximity is the state of being close to something in distance or position.

The hotel's proximity to the station let us walk to every train.

Worked Example

The young lawyer was thrilled to find an apartment in the same block as the courthouse; the proximity to work meant she could walk home in eight minutes during her lunch break.

Proximity is more precise than 'closeness' here because it emphasizes not just the distance itself, but the advantage of being near—that being close makes the commute easy and practical. A plain word like 'closeness' would miss that sense of useful benefit.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

closeness: Closeness is the plain, everyday word for being near — the park's closeness to school, the closeness of two desks. Proximity means the same nearness but carries an extra idea: that the short distance matters, bringing a benefit or a real connection worth pointing out.

adjacency: Adjacency is position directly next to something, touching it or sharing its border — two lockers side by side are adjacent. Proximity claims less: things in proximity are close together, but nothing has to touch. A school two blocks from the park has proximity, not adjacency.

vicinity: The vicinity is the area around a place — the streets and shops near the stadium are in its vicinity. It names a zone you can be inside. Proximity is not a zone but a relationship: how near one thing sits to another, especially when that nearness matters.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

distance: wide amount of space between things

remoteness: state of being far away and isolated

Where it sits · how small the gap between them is — separation → distance → nearness → proximity

separation vs. proximity: Separation means things are kept apart entirely, the far opposite end of the scale from proximity.

distance vs. proximity: Distance emphasizes how far apart two things sit, while proximity emphasizes how close together they are.

nearness vs. proximity: Nearness simply says something is close by, but proximity stresses that the closeness matters or brings an advantage.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — proxim-

Root — proxim-: nearest, very near (Latin (proximus, superlative of prope, 'near'))

Suffix — -ity

Suffix — -ity: state or quality of (Latin (-itas))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin proximus meant 'the nearest' — the superlative of prope, 'near.' Add -ity, 'the state of,' and proximity is literally 'the state of being nearest': closeness itself, named as a thing.

Use the root in a new word: approximate

Use the root in a new word: approximate: Give an approximate count of the marbles — a number that comes near the truth without being exact.

Word Choice

formal / neutral

Proximity is most useful when being near carries practical significance—a benefit, a convenience, or a logical connection. For a simple statement of spatial distance, plain words like 'distance' or 'being near' usually work better. Reach for proximity when closeness matters.
